abstract: We study linear swap regret in self-play against all affine self-maps of each player's strategy polytope. Efficient adversarial bounds for this class scale as $\sqrt{T}$. On compact polytopes given by linear inequalities, our deterministic uncoupled dynamics achieve $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\mathrm{poly}(D)T^{1/3})$ cumulative regret, where $D$ is the binary length of the game description. The bound is independent of the number of vertices. In perfect-recall $n$-player extensive-form games with at most $M$ terminal sequences per player, we obtain $\mathcal{O}(n^2M^4\log T)$ regret against all linear deviations, extending the logarithmic trigger-regret bound of Anagnostides, Farina, and Sandholm [AFS23]. This class can strictly contain the trigger deviations [FP23] and consists exactly of the deviations implementable by untimed communication (UTC), in which a player interleaves moves with mediator queries along a separate feasible path [ZFS24]. The proof combines optimistic log-barrier learning on a compact matrix lift with stability of the Gordon fixed point, using treeplex geometry in extensive form.

title: Breaking the Square-Root Barrier for Linear Swap Regret in Polyhedral Games
